result:
The explorer page is written to `/Users/asherperemel/projects/business-idea-search-work/biz/round2/explorer/index.html` (62,104 bytes, one inline script). `node --check` passes on the extracted script. I also ran it from a local static server in the browser pane, in light and dark, at desktop width and at 400px.

**What the page does**
- **Final five:** cards with rank, refined title, one-liner, median and upside per year, head-to-head record and the reason for the rank. Each card opens its journey.
- **Funnel:** two columns of counts computed from the data. The round 1 counts (1,340, 105, 82, 214 = 82+120+12, 25, 12, best score 3.3/10) and round 2 counts (37, 296, 12, 16, 12, 6, 5) match your spec. Rows are clickable and list that stage in the explorer below. The 143 money pools is the one hardcoded number, because it isn't in the data. Bars use a log scale and say so.
- **Contrarian bets:** three cards, each linked to its record. The links resolve by C05, I0175 and the title "Certified Cell" with pool P038.
- **All 1,768 records:** search over title, one-liner, refined title and ids.
  - Filters: round, kind or lens, furthest stage (with an option to include later stages), and verdict.
  - Sort: furthest stage, tournament rank, deep score or title.
  - The list renders 60 at a time with "Show more", and counts update as you filter.
- **Detail panel:** a side panel on desktop and full-screen on phones. It shows only the stages the idea reached, as a vertical timeline.
  - Round 1: origin, tournament with the three judges, competitor check, evolution with parent and offspring links, and deep validation.
  - Round 2: origin, evidence gate, deep validation, head-to-head, war-game, and final rank or "dropped".
  - The war-game stage shows unit economics, first customers as links, quit conditions, founder fit and the 90-day plan.
  - Navigation: Previous and Next, a stage trail, Esc to close, and the idea is encoded in the URL hash.
- **Design contract:** the contract rules are followed (page content only, tokens on `:root`, both dark-theme blocks, `body` background, Google Fonts only, no storage), and a measured contrast check found 0 failures in either theme. Display face is Young Serif, body is Source Sans 3 with tabular figures, and IDs are in IBM Plex Mono. Loading and error states are included, and the error message explains the need to serve over http. At 400px there is no horizontal scroll and the gutter is 16px.

**Judgment calls and caveats**
- **Added things:** I added "evolution pool" and "evidence-gate pick" as stages so offspring, hybrids and round 2 picks don't collapse into "Generated". I also added a viewport meta tag after the title, because without it mobile browsers laid the page out at 980px.
- **No `wargame` flag in the data:** no record carries `wargame: true`, so the war-game stage is matched through `wargames.json` by `cid` instead.
- **`real` field:** I labelled it "Realistic size per year". Its meaning isn't documented.
- **Truncated text in the data:** `explorer_data.json` cuts several fields at fixed lengths, mid-sentence (customer 300 characters, problem and solution 600, why-now and insight 400, deep-validation objections 600, risk and test 300, competitor white space and sharper angle 400). The panel adds an ellipsis and a note where text hit a cap. I can't restore the full text from the page.
- **Order agreement:** the head-to-head stage shows "Order agreement: 52/66" as given, because I couldn't confirm what it means.
- **Design-hook warnings left in place:** the hook reported 7 low-contrast findings, which I believe are false positives. They pair dark-theme text colors with light-theme backgrounds. In-browser contrast checks across about 1,100 text nodes per theme found 0 failures. I did not write an ignore rule, since that creates a config file in the project. The one all-caps finding was the short eyebrow label, which I shortened.
- **Not done:** I did not run the page from `file://` because the browser blocks `fetch` there. The page must be served over http, and the error panel says so.

I wrote the report to `/Users/asherperemel/projects/business-idea-search/reports/Top 5 business ideas 2026.md`. By `wc -w` it is about 9,040 words, and about 8,500 once table pipes and URLs are excluded.
1. The BLUF and a ten-line answer lead the report: C10 Signed-Off v2, C13 Run-Base Shrinker v2, C03 HCBS Operations Utility, C16 Regional Partner Group, C09 Stafette, in `final_top5.json` order with no re-ranking. The single conclusion is that the edge is the founder's insider position, and no uncrowded venture-scale slam dunk survived.
2. Section 2 has a 12-stage funnel table built from the log's real counts: 1,340 raw ideas, 105 sent to the competitor check, 82 survivors, 25 finalists, 296 round-2 ideas, 12 gate picks, 16 deep-validated, 12 contenders, 6 war-gamed, 5 final. It also states what each filter killed and why.
3. Section 3 gives each idea a full block: pitch, dated and sourced why-now, demand evidence, strongest war-game rival and edge, unit economics, a 10-row first-customer table with URLs, riskiest assumption and the exact test, 90-day plan, dated quit table, founding team, and an honest verdict. Two Stafette customer rows (Altonaer Spar- und Bauverein, degewo) carry no URL because the notes recorded none, and I marked them "no URL recorded".
4. Sections 4-6 and a short conclusion cover three labeled-unvalidated contrarian bets (C05 foundry, Certified Cell, Evac Cash), lessons on finding ideas, and limitations: adversarial-agent bias, LLM judges, desk research only, and no customer calls.
5. I checked that all 95 inline URLs appear verbatim in the notes, so none were invented. Where a source was only a search summary or snippet, the report says so. I used no emojis or em dashes.
